# SOP-P3-L4-02 Product changeover - Heat Treat line

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P3, line P3-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L4-RR01, EQ-P3-L4-HT02, EQ-P3-L4-SB03  
Related documents: MM-P3-L4-RR01-S3, MM-P3-L4-SB03, SB-1019

Purpose
1. This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) defines the steps required to perform a product changeover on the Heat Treat line at P3-L4, covering roll refeed (EQ-P3-L4-RR01), heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02), and shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03). It ensures consistent setup, protects equipment life, and preserves product quality.

Background and Rationale
2. Changeovers are critical operations where incorrect sequences or undocumented adjustments cause rework or equipment damage. This SOP captures the approved sequence and required verification points to reduce variability. Example rationale: confirming feed and restraint positions on EQ-P3-L4-RR01 prevents misalignment through EQ-P3-L4-HT02, and controlled cleaning/finish settings on EQ-P3-L4-SB03 prevent surface contamination prior to inspection.

Preconditions (must be verified before any step)
3. Verify the line is in Planned Downtime and that the previous production lot has completed all hold points. Confirm authorization from shift lead. Confirm availability of required consumables and tooling for the next product run. Review MM-P3-L4-RR01-S3 and MM-P3-L4-SB03 for maintenance status and any open work orders before starting. Confirm no outstanding safety tags on EQ-P3-L4-RR01, EQ-P3-L4-HT02, or EQ-P3-L4-SB03 by checking the line board and SB-1019.

Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)
4. Required PPE for all steps: safety glasses, steel-toe footwear, hearing protection, heat-resistant gloves for furnace areas, and a long-sleeve flame-resistant outer garment while accessing EQ-P3-L4-HT02 service panels. Use respiratory protection as specified in MM-P3-L4-SB03 when working inside the shot blast cabinet area.

Step-by-step Changeover Procedure
5. Tag-in and pre-start checks
   5.1. Sign the changeover authorization in the line changeover log.  
   5.2. Confirm that EQ-P3-L4-RR01, EQ-P3-L4-HT02, and EQ-P3-L4-SB03 are powered to Safe state as required by SB-1019 before performing mechanical adjustments.  
   5.3. Visually inspect tooling and fixtures for wear or foreign material. If any abnormality is present, refer to MM-P3-L4-RR01-S3 for repair procedures.

6. Material handling and fixture setup on EQ-P3-L4-RR01
   6.1. Install the new product fixtures and validate clamp engagement visually.  
   6.2. Jog the feed mechanism slowly to confirm parts seat correctly and that there is no interference with adjacent fixtures.  
   6.3. Verify sensor alignment and presence; if any sensor fault is detected, log the fault and escalate to maintenance per MM-P3-L4-RR01-S3.

7. Heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02) configuration and verification
   7.1. Confirm that furnace internal load carriers are set per product tooling layout and that carriers are secure.  
   7.2. Verify control program selection for the new product on the operator console. Do not adjust control recipes unless authorized by the process engineer.  
   7.3. The quench delay maximum for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P3-L4-HT02) is 20 seconds. Ensure the furnace control confirms the quench delay parameter is at or below this value before first heat. If a discrepancy exists, abort start and notify maintenance.

8. Shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) preparation
   8.1. Confirm abrasive media is appropriate and the cabinet internals are free of buildup. Follow cleaning steps in MM-P3-L4-SB03 for cabinet inspection.  
   8.2. Install and verify the lubricant specified: The lubricant part number for Heat Treat shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P3-L4-SB03) is CFW-LUB-526. Use only this approved part for any pre-blast lubrication operations.  
   8.3. Run a single dry cycle with no parts to confirm blast pattern and media feed. If pattern is non-uniform, consult MM-P3-L4-SB03 for troubleshooting.

9. Dry run and first-piece verification
   9.1. Execute a dry run through EQ-P3-L4-RR01 into EQ-P3-L4-HT02 and through EQ-P3-L4-SB03 with carriers only to confirm material flow and absence of mechanical interference.  
   9.2. Run the first production piece and perform dimensional, visual, and surface-finish checks per product control plan. Record inspection results in the lot start record. If the first-piece inspection fails, stop the line and follow containment steps.

10. Documentation and records to keep
   10.1. Complete the Changeover Checklist and attach copies of first-piece inspection, furnace log printout showing the quench delay parameter, and shot blast setup sheet referencing CFW-LUB-526.  
   10.2. Record any maintenance actions and reference work orders in the maintenance log; cross-reference SB-1019 for safety tag clearances.  
   10.3. Keep records in the electronic Document Control repository and local line binder for traceability.

Examples and common nonconformance scenarios
11. Example: If the quench delay reads above the permitted setting for EQ-P3-L4-HT02, the item must not proceed to quench. Notify maintenance and hold the load until corrected. Log the event and attach furnace control screenshots.  
12. Example: If a non-approved lubricant is found in EQ-P3-L4-SB03, quarantine any affected parts, clean per MM-P3-L4-SB03, and note corrective action.

Process safety and escalation
13. Any equipment alarm or unexpected actuation requires immediate stop of the changeover and notification of the shift supervisor. Follow SB-1019 procedures for lockout/tagout if manual servicing is required. Maintenance approvals per MM-P3-L4-RR01-S3 or MM-P3-L4-SB03 are required prior to restart.

Sign-off and authorization
14. Signatures required to release the line for production:
   14.1. Operator completing changeover — print name and sign.  
   14.2. Shift lead verification — print name and sign after confirming all preconditions and first-piece acceptance.  
   14.3. Maintenance representative — print name and sign if any adjustments were made to EQ-P3-L4-RR01, EQ-P3-L4-HT02, or EQ-P3-L4-SB03 during changeover.

Change history and document control
15. This SOP is controlled in the Document Control system. Refer to MM-P3-L4-RR01-S3 and MM-P3-L4-SB03 for equipment-specific maintenance instructions and to SB-1019 for safety procedures.
